original_question: For graphs that are close to trees, such as graphs with few cycles or sparse graphs of large diameter, is there a structural characterization of the minimum-cardinality (n-k)-contingent zero-forcing sets, meaning vertex sets that remain zero-forcing after any deletion of at most k edges?
target_in_paper: Open Problem 7.1 in Section 7, “(n − k)-contingent zero-forcing for power grids.” ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the paper’s structural, not algorithmic or probabilistic, question: it asks for a characterization of minimal-sized resilient zero-forcing sets, and it names the same two graph families that the paper singles out—graphs with few cycles and sparse graphs with large diameter. Your gloss of an (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing set as one that survives deletion of any at most k edges is also faithful to Definition 7.3. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))
missing_details: The paper’s official target is not the broader phrase “graphs close to trees”; it asks separately about “graphs with few cycles” and “sparse graphs with large diameter.” ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

To be stand-alone, the question should fix a graph G = (V, E) and an integer k ≥ 1, rather than leaving k implicit inside the notation “(n − k)-contingent.” ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

It should explicitly define a zero-forcing move: from a blue set S, a vertex v can be forced if some blue vertex s has N(s) \ S = {v}. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

It should explicitly define a zero-forcing set: a set Z ⊆ V from which some sequence of zero-forcing moves colors all vertices of G. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

It should formalize the contingency condition as: for every E' ⊆ E with |E'| ≤ k, the same set Z is a zero-forcing set of G' = (V, E \ E'). ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

“Minimum-cardinality” should be clarified as minimum cardinality among all (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing sets of the given graph, matching the paper’s phrase “minimal-sized.” ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

The nearby context that motivates the question should be kept in view: for trees, the paper already gives an exact characterization—Z is (n − k)-contingent iff Z contains all vertices of degree at most k—so the open problem is asking for an analogue beyond trees, not for trees themselves. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))
refined_question: Let G = (V, E) be a graph and let k ≥ 1. A zero-forcing move from a blue set S ⊆ V colors a vertex v ∈ V \ S blue if there exists s ∈ S with N(s) \ S = {v}; a set Z ⊆ V is a zero-forcing set if some sequence of zero-forcing moves colors all vertices of G. Following Definition 7.3, call Z an (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing set if for every edge set E' ⊆ E with |E'| ≤ k, Z is a zero-forcing set of G' = (V, E \ E'). For graphs with few cycles, and separately for sparse graphs with large diameter, is there a structural characterization of the (n − k)-contingent zero-forcing sets of minimum cardinality? ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by Lemma 7.7, for graphs with few cycles, and separately for sparse graphs with large diameter, is there a structural characterization of the minimum-cardinality k-leaky zero-forcing sets, where Z ⊆ V is k-leaky if for every L ⊆ V with |L| ≤ k, Z is a zero-forcing set of the graph obtained from G by attaching a pendant vertex to each vertex of L? ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly aiming at Open Problem 7.1 in Section 7, not at Open Problem 7.2 (efficient algorithm) or Open Problem 7.3 (typical size), because it asks for a “structural characterization” of minimal-size resilient forcing sets. The relevant nearby definitions are Definition 7.1 (zero-forcing move), Definition 7.2 (zero-forcing set), and Definition 7.3 ((n − k)-contingent zero forcing). The immediate context also matters: Theorem 7.4 and Lemma 7.5 explain that trees are already solved exactly, which is why the paper next asks for graphs with few cycles and sparse graphs with large diameter. Lemma 7.7 gives the only explicit equivalent reformulation nearby, namely equivalence with k-leaky zero forcing. No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, polynomial degree, or nilpotency hypotheses are relevant here, because this target is purely graph-theoretic. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))
